environment.description: Same IoT gateway binary deployed behind an industrial protocol-aware message broker (Eclipse Mosquitto 2.0.18 with custom auth plugin). Telemetry ingestion occurs via MQTT with max message size enforced at broker level (max_packet_size 16384 in mosquitto.conf). The web dashboard is served through an nginx 1.25.3 reverse proxy with Content-Security-Policy header that includes script-src directives with require-sri-for enforcement AND specific integrity attributes baked into the nginx sub_filter rewrite module. Specifically, nginx sub_filter rewrites all <script src=...> tags to inject integrity='sha384-<precomputed-hash>' crossorigin='anonymous' attributes before forwarding to client. The nginx config uses 'sub_filter_once off' with pattern matching on '<script src=' to prepend the SRI attribute from a maintained allowlist hash map (njs module sri_inject.js). Additionally, the CSP header includes 'require-sri-for script' directive. The MQTT broker's max_packet_size=16384 constraint means the payload_count * payload_size product that triggers the integer overflow (requiring total raw message > 64KB to be exploitable) cannot physically arrive at the handler - the broker silently drops oversized PUBLISH packets per MQTT 5.0 spec section 3.3.2.3.4.

nginx_config.csp_header: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://cdn.iotgateway.internal 'require-sri-for script'; style-src 'self'
nginx_config.sri_injection: njs module sri_inject.js rewrites script tags with sha384 integrity attributes from allowlist
